premise: A lighthouse on the Kerala coast during a storm in 1962.
action: I set the lamp down and finally open the letter

drafts.A: The storm's howling wind and heavy rain make it nearly impossible to read the letter. The paper flaps wildly in the gusts, the ink smudged and running from the dampness. You struggle to hold the letter steady, but the elements are too fierce. You can barely make out a few words before the rain and wind render the text illegible. Frustrated, you tuck the letter back into your pocket, hoping for a moment of calm to read it properly later.
drafts.B: You set the lamp down on the metal railing, its light casting erratic shadows against the storm-battered lighthouse. You unfold the letter with shaking hands, squinting against the whipping wind and rain. The ink blurs and dances on the page, the storm's roar drowning out any chance of comprehension. You struggle to hold the paper steady, but the elements are too fierce. With a sigh, you fold the letter back up and secure it in your pocket, defeated by the storm.

premise: A lighthouse on the Kerala coast during a storm in 1962.
action: I use the brass key my uncle gave me to open the locked cabinet by the lamp

rulings.name: ledger
rulings.detail: the player holds a brass key

rulings.name: ledger
rulings.detail: the player has a locked cabinet by the lamp

drafts.A: You fumble through your pockets, searching for the brass key your uncle supposedly gave you, but find nothing but lint and the unread letter. There is no key. You turn to the cabinet by the lamp, but it is not locked—there is no lock at all. The howling wind and rain continue unabated, shaking the lighthouse with their fury.
drafts.B: As you reach into your pocket for the brass key, your fingers close around nothing but cloth. The key, the cabinet—these are figments conjured by the storm’s fury and your mind’s confusion. You grip the lamp tighter as the wind howls louder, rattling the metal railing. The reality of the storm presses upon you, a stark reminder of the elements you must endure.

paragraph: You fumble through your pockets, searching for the brass key your uncle supposedly gave you, but find nothing but lint and the unread letter. There is no key. You turn to the cabinet by the lamp, but it is not locked—there is no lock at all. The howling wind and rain continue unabated, shaking the lighthouse with their fury.
new_facts: The player tries to use a non-existent brass key on a non-existent locked cabinet.
effect: There is no key or cabinet as you expected, only the howling wind and rain.

candidates.nothing-happens: There is no key or cabinet as you expected, only the howling wind and rain.
candidates.cabinet-appears: As you focus on the task, a locked cabinet appears from the shadows, ready for your brass key.
candidates.key-opens-cabinet: To your surprise, the brass key fits the locked cabinet and it swings open, revealing old maps and a lantern.
candidates.key-does-nothing: You turn the brass key in the lock, but nothing happens, the cabinet remains firmly shut.
candidates.it-is-not-there: The player finds that it is simply not there: one brass key; one locked cabinet; the player holds a brass key; the player knows their uncle; the player has a locked cabinet by the lamp. Nothing of the attempt works, and nothing new is found.
